headline: Tax-season strength lifts revenue and profit
summary_short: Revenue rose 5.3% y/y to $2,398.1M in H&R Block's seasonally heaviest quarter (three months ended March 31, 2026), with net income up 17.4% y/y to $847.9M as a lower 16.5% effective tax rate — driven by an $84.1M IRS settlement benefit — lifted earnings well ahead of the 6.0% growth in operating income.
summary_long: Revenue grew 5.3% y/y to $2,398.1M (+$121.0M) on higher net average charge and tax-return volume, plus 16.0% international growth from favorable FX. Operating income rose 6.0% y/y to $1,036.8M as revenue growth outpaced a $62.5M rise in field wages, benefits and occupancy costs. Net income rose faster, +17.4% y/y to $847.9M, after the effective tax rate fell to 16.5% from 24.6% on an $84.1M discrete benefit from settling a 2020 IRS examination. Diluted EPS was $6.60 (GAAP, +24.3% y/y) and $6.02 (non-GAAP, +11.9% y/y). Long-term debt fell to $1,490.9M from $2,435.4M sequentially as tax-season cash repaid revolver borrowings; no shares were repurchased this quarter. Results are highly seasonal — the company states interim quarters aren't representative of full-year performance.

drivers.explanation: U.S. assisted tax preparation revenue rose $106.3M (+6.5%) on a 3.8% increase in net average charge and 2.6% more company-owned tax-return volume; international revenue grew 16.0% on favorable FX in Canada and Australia.
Tracks the same field-wage, benefits, and occupancy cost growth the filing cites for total operating expenses; the 10-Q does not break out a cost-of-revenue-specific cause separately.
Revenue grew $121.0M while total operating expenses grew a smaller $62.5M (field wages +$44.6M, benefits +$6.6M, occupancy +$7.6M, partly offset by lower marketing spend), so income expanded.
Moves with operating income; the same $121.0M revenue gain against a smaller $62.5M opex increase explains the rise.
Follows EBIT plus a stable D&A add-back; the company's own reconciliation table shows a $60.2M y/y EBITDA gain (+5.9%).
Tracks operating income's growth; the filing gives no pretax-specific cause beyond the revenue and expense trends already discussed.

The effective tax rate fell to 16.5% from 24.6% on an $84.1M discrete tax benefit from settling an IRS examination of the 2020 return, lifting net income growth (+17.4%) well above operating income growth (+6.0%).
Tracks net income's growth; a smaller basic share count from ongoing buybacks (126.8M vs 133.9M shares) added modest additional per-share upside.
Tracks net income's growth; the decrease in weighted average shares outstanding is due to share repurchases completed in the current and prior fiscal years.
Non-GAAP EPS excludes discrete tax impacts, acquisition-related intangible amortization and goodwill impairments from GAAP EPS, per the company's own reconciliation table.

Nine-month operating cash flow of $586.7M (on higher net income and working-capital timing) exceeded $122.6M of investing outflows and $579.5M of financing outflows (dividends, debt service), consistent with the tax-season cash build.
Nine-month cash flow shows $2,375.0M of line-of-credit repayments funded by tax-season cash inflows, consistent with paying down the seasonal borrowing peak reached in the prior (off-season) quarter.

Deficit narrowed as the quarter's $847.9M net income flowed into retained earnings against $53.2M of dividends declared and only $41 thousand of treasury-share activity — no open-market buybacks this quarter.
The decrease in the weighted average shares outstanding is due to share repurchases completed in the current and prior fiscal years.

Higher net average charge, tax-return volume growth, and favorable international FX drove revenue and earnings higher y/y, while an IRS settlement's tax-rate benefit lifted net income well beyond operating income growth; the company flags interim results as seasonal and not representative of the full year.
